jobs.title: Vice President of Enrollment Management
jobs.description: Franklin Switzerland, founded in 1969, is one of the first institutions to bring liberal arts education to Europe and to be recognized by both U.S. and Swiss accreditation agencies. A leader in international education, Franklin provides an experiential and multinational learning environment through small classes, strong student and faculty relationships, a residential campus, and hands-on Academic Travel experiences. With roughly 300 students from more than 55 countries, set in the safe and striking landscape of Lugano, Franklin is distinctive: an intimate residential community, a uniquely dual U.S.–Swiss accreditation, and an Academic Travel program that turns the world into a classroom. Franklin promotes intellectual curiosity and critical thinking, strives for academic excellence, and fosters interdisciplinary opportunities for its students, faculty, and staff. Franklin acknowledges the accomplishments and global impact of our community through a culture of trust that respects representation from a variety of backgrounds, as well as an environment that strives for continuous improvement. THE OPPORTUNITY Franklin Switzerland is seeking an accomplished, hands-on, and strategically minded Vice President of Enrollment Management (VPEM) to help lead student recruitment, admissions operations, financial-aid coordination, and enrollment growth at a pivotal moment for the University. This is an important institutional role for someone who understands both the human and analytical sides of enrollment. Franklin needs a person who can think strategically, act practically, manage people and processes, work comfortably with data, and remain close to the daily work of recruitment and conversion. The successful candidate will bring energy, judgment, discipline, and a genuine belief in the value of a Franklin education. The VPEM will work closely with the President, senior leadership, Admissions, Financial Aid, Marketing and Communications, Academic Affairs, Student Affairs, Finance, faculty, staff, students, external partners, agents, and school counselors to support Franklin’s enrollment goals across undergraduate, graduate, transfer, visiting, study abroad, and partnership pathways. This is not a role for someone who wants only to supervise from a distance. It requires a leader who can build systems, coach staff, review data, improve communication flows, speak with families, support recruitment travel, solve practical problems, and help move prospective students from interest to enrollment. Franklin is looking for a VPEM who is genuinely fluent across the enrollment cycle and who can hold three priorities in balance: Recruitment and conversion — building a disciplined, warm, and responsive admissions operation that supports students and families from first inquiry through application, admission, deposit, visa, arrival, and handoff to the student experience. Data and systems — using Slate, funnel reports, dashboards, segmentation, and timely analysis to identify opportunities, address weaknesses, improve conversion, and support evidence-based enrollment decisions. Collaboration and execution — working across departments to ensure that Franklin’s distinctive academic, residential, and international identity is translated into clear recruitment messages, effective campaigns, strong events, and a consistent prospective-student experience. The ideal candidate understands that enrollment management is both strategic and practical. Students and families make decisions over time, through many interactions, questions, doubts, comparisons, and moments of reassurance. Franklin must be visible, compelling, responsive, credible, and operationally excellent throughout that journey. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Enrollment Strategy & Planning ▪ Support the development, implementation, and evaluation of a comprehensive enrollment management plan aligned with Franklin’s mission, academic priorities, financial realities, and strategic goals. ▪ Translate enrollment goals into practical recruitment plans, territory strategies, communication flows, event calendars, staff priorities, funnel targets, and measurable outcomes. ▪ Monitor enrollment trends, application behavior, deposit patterns, yield indicators, market conditions, and competitor activity, and recommend timely adjustments. ▪ Work closely with senior leadership to support short- and long-term enrollment planning, including undergraduate, graduate, transfer, visiting, study abroad, and partnership enrollment. ▪ Contribute to regular enrollment reporting for the President, senior leadership, relevant committees, and other internal stakeholders. ▪ Help foster a campus-wide culture of enrollment awareness, shared responsibility, openness, and precision. Recruitment, Admissions & Yield ▪ Lead and support the admissions recruitment team in achieving inquiry, application, admit, deposit, and enrollment goals. ▪ Oversee the prospective-student journey from inquiry to enrollment, ensuring timely, professional, warm, and persuasive communication with students, families, counselors, agents, and partners. ▪ Strengthen recruitment practices, admissions processes, territory management, school counselor outreach, campus visits, virtual engagement, admitted-student yield, and pre-arrival communication. ▪ Personally engage in recruitment activity where needed, including conversations with prospective students and families, school visits, fairs, partner meetings, admitted-student events, and yield initiatives. ▪ Work closely with Marketing and Communications to ensure that recruitment campaigns, landing pages, email flows, social content, events, and digital outreach are aligned with enrollment priorities and Franklin’s distinctive identity. ▪ Support strategies to grow enrollment across specific programs and markets, and to sustain Franklin's signature multinational classroom, often 15–20 nationalities represented in a single course, by recruiting broadly across countries and regions and by broadening access for students from a range of socioeconomic backgrounds. ▪ Contribute to the development of study abroad, visiting-student, transfer, and institutional partnership pipelines. ▪ Regular travel may be required, including recruitment travel, school visits, fairs, conferences, partner meetings, and engagement with students, families, counselors, agents, alumni, and institutional partners in Switzerland, Europe, the United States, and other relevant markets. Financial Aid & Affordability ▪ Work closely with the Director of Financial Aid to ensure that financial-aid processes are timely, clear, student-centered, compliant, and aligned with enrollment goals. ▪ Support financial-aid and scholarship strategies that balance access, affordability, yield, net tuition revenue, discount rate, and institutional sustainability. ▪ Help analyze financial-aid data, award behavior, yield patterns, family concerns, and affordability barriers to support improved enrollment outcomes. ▪ Ensure that students and families receive accurate, clear, and supportive guidance on cost, aid, payment expectations, and the value of a Franklin education. ▪ Partner with Finance and senior leadership as needed to support enrollment forecasting, financial-aid modeling, and net revenue analysis. Data, Slate & Enrollment Operations ▪ Use Slate and other enrollment technologies to support recruitment, admissions processing, communications, reporting, events, application review, and yield management. ▪ Develop and maintain clear enrollment dashboards, funnel reports, conversion analyses, and regular performance updates. ▪ Ensure that data quality, coding, source tracking, communication rules, forms, workflows, and reporting structures support accurate analysis and effective decision-making. ▪ Recommend and implement process improvements to increase speed, clarity, responsiveness, user experience, data quality, and access to services. ▪ Collaborate with the Slate Manager and relevant colleagues to improve automation, communication plans, event management, application workflows, and recruitment reporting. ▪ Identify positive and negative performance trends and propose practical action plans to strengthen results. Team Leadership & Collaboration ▪ Supervise, support, and develop members of the admissions recruitment team and other enrollment staff as assigned. ▪ Establish clear expectations, priorities, accountability structures, and service standards for the team. ▪ Build a high-trust, high-performance culture that is student-centered, collaborative, data-aware, resilient, and focused on results. ▪ Provide regular feedback, coaching, and practical support to staff, while modeling the energy, responsiveness, and professionalism expected of the team. ▪ Work closely with colleagues across Marketing, Financial Aid, Student Affairs, Academic Affairs, Finance, Advancement, faculty, and external partners. ▪ Represent Franklin with professionalism, warmth, humility, and credibility in internal and external settings. Budget & Resource Stewardship ▪ Assist with the development and administration of enrollment-related budgets, including recruitment travel, events, systems, agencies, and other departmental expenditures. ▪ Link spending recommendations to measurable enrollment outcomes and institutional priorities. ▪ Evaluate the effectiveness of recruitment activities, travel, fairs, events, campaigns, platforms, agents, and partnerships. ▪ Seek practical and creative ways to achieve enrollment goals with limited resources, balancing ambition with disciplined execution. ▪ Perform other duties as assigned, consistent with this position, the department’s goals, and the University’s mission. EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS Franklin is seeking an experienced enrollment leader with a minimum of 7–10 years of progressive experience in higher education enrollment management, admissions, recruitment, financial aid, or a closely related area, including at least 3–5 years in a senior, supervisory, or team leadership role. The successful candidate will be required to have earned a bachelor’s degree; an advanced degree is strongly preferred. In addition, the successful candidate will possess the following: ▪ Recruitment fluency — Direct understanding of the full student recruitment cycle, including territory management, family engagement, counselor relationships, campus visits, recruitment events, admitted-student yield, conversion strategy, and undergraduate and graduate pipelines. ▪ Strategic and practical orientation — Demonstrated ability to help develop and execute strategic enrollment plans, particularly in a small or mid-sized institution, while also managing the daily work required to implement them effectively. ▪ Data competence — Demonstrated ability to use enrollment data, funnel reports, CRM systems, dashboards, segmentation, business intelligence tools, and conversion analysis to guide decisions, evaluate performance, and improve outcomes. ▪ Slate experience — Experience with Slate is strongly preferred. Experience with comparable CRM, student recruitment, or enrollment management systems will also be considered. ▪ Financial-aid awareness — Working knowledge of financial aid, scholarship strategy, affordability concerns, discounting, yield behavior, financial aid leveraging, discount rate modeling, and the relationship between enrollment and institutional finances. ▪ Team leadership — Proven ability to supervise, motivate, coach, and hold accountable collaborative, high-performing staff in a fast-moving and service-oriented environment, including teams working across multiple locations or time zones. ▪ Communication skills — Excellent written and oral communication skills in English are required. Proficiency in Italian, French, German, Spanish, Arabic, or another relevant language is an asset. ▪ International outlook — Experience with international recruitment, U.S. higher education, Swiss or European markets, study-abroad partnerships, globally mobile students, or transnational education is a strong advantage. ▪ Liberal arts understanding — Familiarity with the liberal arts college market and the ability to articulate its value proposition to prospective students and families is strongly preferred. Key Competencies for Franklin Leaders ▪ Strategic thinking ▪ Practical execution ▪ Leading and inspiring ▪ Self-awareness ▪ Data-informed decision-making ▪ Cross-cultural communication ▪ Student-centered service ▪ Collaboration ▪ Effectiveness ▪ Continuously evolving FRANKLIN SWITZERLAND Mission The mission of Franklin Switzerland is to provide a cross-cultural and multinational learning and living environment that inspires students to engage the world. We challenge students through a curriculum that integrates the liberal arts with professional pathways, and classroom learning with Academic Travel to destinations around the world. A Franklin education produces critical thinkers who are culturally literate, ethically aware and intellectually courageous. We prepare students to become responsible, compassionate, and collaborative leaders in an increasingly complex and interconnected world. History It was the end of the sixties, and Fleming College, a program of The American School in Switzerland, was closing its doors. Four of its faculty, Theo Brenner, Wilfried Geens, Pascal Tone and Jacques Villaret teamed up with the chair of Fleming’s European board to found a new higher education institution named after Benjamin Franklin. They believed that by providing international experiences to students, Franklin College would strengthen the relationships between members of different nations and cultures. Pascal Tone spent the summer of 1970 recruiting the first class in New York City while the others completed preparation of the first campus at Villa Cirla, an 18th century building in Lugano. That year, Franklin employed 10 faculty and offered 36 courses under 4 subjects: Study of Civilizations, Art, Politics and Economics, and Languages and Literature. David R. Grace served as First Chairman of the Board. During the seventies, Franklin moved to Villa Ferrari and then to Villa Sassa, where it was first accredited as a two-year college by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education (MSCHE). In 1986 Franklin College Switzerland finally took residence in its permanent campus on Via Ponte Tresa in Sorengo. In that same year it was accredited as a four-year college by the MSCHE. The new millennium brought new growth, as the entire academic and administrative community sought to define a new future for Franklin. In 2005, Franklin's undergraduate programs received accreditation from the Swiss University Conference, and in 2006, the college expanded to a second campus formerly occupied by the Leonardo DaVinci school. In 2010, Franklin’s first master’s degree program was created. 2013 saw Franklin receive full institutional accreditation from the Swiss University Conference, making it a recognized higher education institution within the Swiss university system and the only higher education institution in the world fully accredited in both the US and Switzerland. In 2023, Franklin opened the McNeely Center of Ideas & Imagination and the Giardino di Luce. Named after Rosemary McNeely and Kevin W. McNeely ’73, Trustee, the Center offers a space for students to engage and strengthen their interdisciplinary and experiential education at Franklin. Providing a highly visible face for the University, the facade represents the exterior of a book, an ode to education and learning, and includes many living and learning areas for the Franklin community. The ground floor’s P. Gregory Warden Student Center, comprises a lounge area with comfortable, modular furniture, allowing students to come together, study, and relax. The Giardino di Luce, or Garden of Light, created and donated by Nora McNeely Hurley ’81, is a special wellness garden filled with more than 24 types of lush local flora in the naturally terraced slope. The garden encompasses a space between all three residences and serves as a holistic learning environment. Since its opening, the McNeely Center of Ideas & Imagination has become a vibrant hub on campus. In 2025, Franklin officially renamed itself and became Franklin Switzerland. From the beginning of the four founders believing in their idea to create a new kind of higher education, Franklin now occupies 9 buildings, including 6 residence halls, and teaches students from over 55 countries majoring in any of 19 disciplines on two connected campuses. The fundamental values, however, have always remained the same: personalized learning through interactions both inside and outside of the classroom, true understanding of people and cultures through direct contact and guided travel, and active engagement with the world as an imperative of global, liberal education. Academic & Student Life Franklin Switzerland offers a sense of community, unforgettable student-professor interactions, a breathtaking campus, endless opportunities deriving from its central location in Europe, unique academic experiences inside and outside of the classroom, the exposure and integration of student cultures, and a strong global alumni network. Franklin students originate from 60 different countries. As a result, becoming a Franklin student means studying in a global environment while living in the heart of Europe and connecting with people worldwide as a student, not as a tourist. Franklin provides an incredible academic experience that will contribute to each student’s personal and professional growth. Switzerland has four national languages—German, French, Italian, and Romansh—but English is widely spoken, particularly in universities, international businesses, and major cities. All academic programs at Franklin Switzerland are taught entirely in English. At the same time, students are encouraged to develop proficiency in one of Switzerland's national languages, strengthening both their cultural understanding and career opportunities. At Franklin Switzerland, students have a unique set of academic opportunities, starting with Franklin’s signature program, Academic Travel. Academic Travel blends classroom preparation with the opportunity to study with professors in a different country for two weeks every semester. That isn’t the only thing that sets Franklin apart, however. Professors use real-world experiences to teach the practical skills students need in their careers. Franklin hosts industry experts to interactively discuss current and emerging trends. Franklin’s international faculty and student body provide an immersive environment of cross-cultural perspectives. Every moment spent on campus, whether studying or relaxing, becomes a learning experience. Franklin offers multicultural events, clubs, and activities to help students grow international competence and confidence. What’s more, Franklin offers opportunities for honors students, for students who may need some additional preparation, and for displaced persons needing additional support to begin or continue university study. Franklin Switzerland offers students a unique and dynamic learning environment, where education goes beyond traditional boundaries. Undergraduates can explore a myriad of major fields of study that are deeply intertwined with an interdisciplinary and experiential approach. Its diverse array of majors incorporates various disciplines such as international relations, environmental studies, economics, and art, allowing students to receive a holistic and globally oriented education. The flexibility of the curriculum enables students to shape their academic journey, intertwining their interests and career aspirations. At Franklin Switzerland, they believe in the transformative power of combining academic theory with real-world practice. Its interdisciplinary approach ensures that students explore subjects from multiple perspectives, fostering critical thinking, problem-solving, and a deeper understanding of global issues. The experiential learning components allow students to engage in practical experiences, internships, and field studies, connecting classroom knowledge to real-world applications and enhancing their professional readiness. LOCATION Lugano The Franklin campus is located on a hillside in Sorengo, above the city of Lugano, in the south of Switzerland. Nestled in the Italian-speaking region, students, faculty, and staff can enjoy a Mediterranean atmosphere while remaining connected to major European cities. The city exudes Italian charm; the Mediterranean lifestyle on Lake Lugano, in combination with the surrounding mountains, make Lugano a popular destination. Lugano is the cultural, recreational, financial, and commercial hub of Switzerland’s southernmost, Italian-speaking canton of Ticino, the ideal melting pot of European culture combined with the traits of a small town. It is fun, sophisticated and safe, with dozens of outdoor activities around Lake Lugano, including 40 of Europe’s best mountain bike routes. Residents can enjoy the city center with Mediterranean-style squares and arcades, numerous parks and every variety of shops and restaurants, as well as the LAC Lugano Arte e Cultura, Lugano’s new Arts Center where visual arts, music and performing arts come together in a single venue so as to provide the best experience of art in every form. These and other renowned events attract visitors from all over Europe. As a result, French, German and English are likely to be heard on the streets, in addition to the city’s native Italian. Lugano is the central point of departure for all of Europe. With Lugano’s rail lines and regional airport, all of Europe is within easy reach. Only an hour’s travel from Lugano is Milan, the commercial center of northern Italy — and with a few additional hours, reach Venice, Florence, Strasbourg, Nice, and Innsbruck. Switzerland Located in the heart of Europe, Switzerland borders Italy, France, Germany, Austria, and Liechtenstein. One of the most beautiful countries in the world with its striking mountains and breathtaking landscapes, Switzerland is recognized worldwide for its innovation, political stability, outstanding education system, and exceptional quality of life. Switzerland is also consistently ranked among the safest countries in the world, offering a high quality of life and excellent public services. Its well-organized infrastructure and low crime rates make it an attractive destination. As a cultural melting pot with four official languages (German, French, Italian, and Romansh), an advocate of global participation, and a well-known hub for efficiency, Switzerland is a great choice for professionals seeking to move abroad. COMPENSATION Franklin Switzerland offers a competitive compensation package, including relocation assistance, and a salary commensurate with qualifications and experience. The range identified for this role is 130,000 – 150,000 Swiss Francs / 160,000 – 185,000 US Dollars. This is a full-time, on-campus position based in Lugano, Switzerland. Applicants can expect a welcoming, international, and intercultural working and academic environment, filled with a strong sense of companionship and belonging. Offers of employment will be conditional upon satisfactory results of a background check. TO APPLY NES, a national executive search firm specializing in higher education, is Franklin Switzerland with this search for a Vice President for Enrollment Management. If you wish to have a confidential conversation about this opportunity or submit nominations, please contact: Laura Robinson (laura.robinson@nessearches.com) or Drew Nichols (drew.nichols@nessearches.com). To apply, please send the following items by email to: franklin@nessearches.com: 1) a resume detailing relevant experience; 2) a letter of interest that addresses the key areas of this job description and explains why Franklin Switzerland is a compelling next step, and 3) contact information for five professional references. For best consideration, all application materials should be submitted electronically by October 14, 2026. All inquiries, nominations, and applications will be handled with the utmost confidentiality, and candidates will be notified before references are contacted. The VPEM’s anticipated start date is no later than January 2027. *Please note that, due to Swiss visa and work-permit regulations, applications from Swiss or EU nationals will be given priority in the evaluation process. Franklin Switzerland is an Equal Opportunity / Affirmative Action employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. For further information, please see Franklin’s website: https://www.fus.edu

descriptionByLocale.it: Franklin Svizzera, fondata nel 1969, è una delle prime istituzioni a portare l'educazione alle arti liberali in Europa e ad essere riconosciuta sia dagli enti di accreditamento statunitensi che svizzeri. Leader nell'educazione internazionale, Franklin fornisce un ambiente di apprendimento esperienziale e multinazionale attraverso piccole classi, forti rapporti studenteschi e docenti, un campus residenziale, e esperienze pratiche di viaggio accademico. Con circa 300 studenti provenienti da più di 55 paesi, ambientati nel paesaggio sicuro e suggestivo di Lugano, Franklin è caratteristico: un'intima comunità residenziale, un'accreditamento dual U.S.–Swiss, e un programma di viaggio accademico che trasforma il mondo in classe. Franklin promuove la curiosità intellettuale e il pensiero critico, si sforza per l'eccellenza accademica, e promuove opportunità interdisciplinari per i suoi studenti, docenti e personale. Franklin riconosce i risultati e l'impatto globale della nostra comunità attraverso una cultura di fiducia che rispetta la rappresentazione da una varietà di background, così come un ambiente che si sforza di migliorare continuamente. L'OPPORTUNITÀ Franklin Svizzera sta cercando un buon, pratico e strategicamente pensato Vice Presidente della Direzione Iscrizioni (VPEM) per aiutare a guidare il reclutamento degli studenti, le operazioni di ammissione, il coordinamento finanziario-aiuto e la crescita di iscrizione in un momento cardine per l'Università. Questo è un ruolo istituzionale importante per qualcuno che comprende sia i lati umani che analitici dell'iscrizione. Franklin ha bisogno di una persona che può pensare strategicamente, agire praticamente, gestire persone e processi, lavorare comodamente con i dati, e rimanere vicino al lavoro quotidiano di reclutamento e conversione. Il candidato di successo porterà energia, giudizio, disciplina e una fede autentica nel valore di un'istruzione Franklin. Il VPEM lavorerà a stretto contatto con il Presidente, la leadership senior, le autorizzazioni, gli aiuti finanziari, il marketing e le comunicazioni, gli affari accademici, gli affari degli studenti, le finanze, la facoltà, il personale, gli studenti, i partner esterni, gli agenti e i consulenti scolastici per sostenere gli obiettivi di iscrizione di Franklin attraverso i percorsi di laurea, laurea, trasferimento, visita, studio all'estero e partenariato. Questo non è un ruolo per qualcuno che vuole solo supervisionare da una distanza. Richiede un leader in grado di costruire sistemi, personale di pullman, rivedere i dati, migliorare i flussi di comunicazione, parlare con le famiglie, sostenere i viaggi di reclutamento, risolvere problemi pratici, e aiutare a spostare gli studenti potenziali da interesse per l'iscrizione. Franklin è alla ricerca di un VPEM che è genuinamente fluente attraverso il ciclo di iscrizione e che può tenere tre priorità in equilibrio: reclutamento e conversione — costruzione di un'operazione di ammissione disciplinata, calda e reattiva che supporta gli studenti e le famiglie dalla prima indagine attraverso l'applicazione, l'ammissione, il deposito, il visto, l'arrivo e il passaggio all'esperienza dello studente. Dati e sistemi — utilizzando Slate, report imbuti, dashboard, segmentazione e analisi tempestive per identificare opportunità, affrontare debolezze, migliorare la conversione e sostenere le decisioni di registrazione basate sulle prove. Collaborazione ed esecuzione — lavorando in tutti i dipartimenti per garantire che l'identità accademica, residenziale e internazionale di Franklin sia tradotto in messaggi di reclutamento chiari, campagne efficaci, eventi forti, e una costante esperienza prospettica-studente. Il candidato ideale comprende che la gestione dell'iscrizione è sia strategica che pratica. Gli studenti e le famiglie prendono decisioni nel tempo, attraverso molte interazioni, domande, dubbi, confronti e momenti di rassicurazione. Franklin deve essere visibile, convincente, reattivo, credibile, e operativamente eccellente durante questo viaggio. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Enrollment Strategy & Planning ▪ Supporta lo sviluppo, l'implementazione e la valutazione di un piano di gestione dell'iscrizione completo allineato con la missione di Franklin, le priorità accademiche, le realtà finanziarie e gli obiettivi strategici. ▪ Tradurre gli obiettivi di iscrizione in piani di reclutamento pratici, strategie del territorio, flussi di comunicazione, calendari eventi, priorità del personale, obiettivi imbuti e risultati misurabili. ▪ Monitorare le tendenze di iscrizione, il comportamento delle applicazioni, i modelli di deposito, gli indicatori di rendimento, le condizioni di mercato e l'attività concorrente, e raccomandare le regolazioni tempestive. ▪ Lavorare a stretto contatto con la leadership senior per sostenere la pianificazione di iscrizione a breve e a lungo termine, tra cui laurea, laurea, trasferimento, visita, studio all'estero, e l'iscrizione di partnership. ▪ Contribuisci alla segnalazione regolare di iscrizione per il Presidente, la leadership senior, i comitati pertinenti e altri stakeholder interni. ▪ Aiuta a promuovere una cultura a livello del campus di consapevolezza dell'iscrizione, responsabilità condivisa, apertura e precisione. Reclutamento, Ammissioni & Yield ▪ Guidare e sostenere il team di assunzione di ammissione nel raggiungimento degli obiettivi di inchiesta, applicazione, ammettere, deposito e iscrizione. ▪ Superare il percorso prospettivo-studente dall'inchiesta all'iscrizione, assicurando una comunicazione tempestiva, professionale, calda e persuasiva con studenti, famiglie, consulenti, agenti e partner. ▪ Rafforzare le pratiche di reclutamento, i processi di ammissione, la gestione del territorio, la formazione del consulente scolastico, le visite del campus, l'impegno virtuale, il rendimento ammesso-studente e la comunicazione pre-arrivo. ▪ Personalmente si impegna in attività di reclutamento dove necessario, tra cui conversazioni con potenziali studenti e famiglie, visite scolastiche, fiere, riunioni di partner, eventi ammessi-studenti e iniziative di rendimento. ▪ Lavorare a stretto contatto con Marketing e Comunicazione per garantire che le campagne di reclutamento, le pagine di sbarco, i flussi di posta elettronica, i contenuti sociali, gli eventi e la digital outreach siano allineati con priorità di iscrizione e l’identità distintiva di Franklin. ▪ Strategie di sostegno per crescere l'iscrizione in programmi e mercati specifici, e per sostenere la classe multinazionale di Franklin, spesso 15-20 nazionalità rappresentate in un unico corso, reclutando in ampia misura in paesi e regioni e ampliando l'accesso agli studenti da una gamma di background socioeconomici. ▪ Contribuire allo sviluppo di studi all'estero, visite-studenti, trasferimenti e contratti di partenariato istituzionali. ▪ Possono essere richiesti viaggi regolari, tra cui viaggi di reclutamento, visite scolastiche, fiere, conferenze, incontri di partner e impegno con studenti, famiglie, consulenti, agenti, alunni e partner istituzionali in Svizzera, Europa, Stati Uniti e altri mercati rilevanti. Financial Aid & Affordability ▪ Lavorare a stretto contatto con il direttore degli aiuti finanziari per garantire che i processi di aiuto finanziario siano tempestivi, chiari, centrati sugli studenti, conformi e allineati agli obiettivi di iscrizione. ▪ Sostenere le strategie di aiuto finanziario e di borsa di studio che bilanciano l'accesso, la convenienza, la resa, le entrate di iscrizione nette, il tasso di sconto e la sostenibilità istituzionale. ▪ Aiuta a analizzare i dati di aiuto finanziario, il comportamento di premio, i modelli di rendimento, le preoccupazioni della famiglia e le barriere di convenienza per sostenere i risultati di iscrizione migliorati. ▪ Assicurarsi che gli studenti e le famiglie ricevano una guida accurata, chiara e solidale su costi, aiuti, aspettative di pagamento e il valore di un'istruzione Franklin. ▪ Partner con finanza e leadership senior come necessario per sostenere la previsione di iscrizione, la modellazione finanziaria-aiuto e l'analisi di ricavi netti. Dati, operazioni di registro e registrazione ▪ Utilizzare Slate e altre tecnologie di registrazione per supportare il reclutamento, l'elaborazione delle ammissioni, le comunicazioni, la segnalazione, gli eventi, la revisione delle applicazioni e la gestione dei rendimenti. ▪ Sviluppare e mantenere chiare dashboard di iscrizione, report imbuto, analisi di conversione e aggiornamenti regolari delle prestazioni. ▪ Assicurarsi che la qualità dei dati, la codifica, il monitoraggio delle fonti, le regole di comunicazione, i moduli, i flussi di lavoro e le strutture di report supportano l'analisi accurata e il processo decisionale efficace. ▪ Raccomanda e implementa i miglioramenti del processo per aumentare la velocità, la chiarezza, la reattività, l'esperienza utente, la qualità dei dati e l'accesso ai servizi. ▪ Collabora con Slate Manager e colleghi rilevanti per migliorare l'automazione, i piani di comunicazione, la gestione degli eventi, i flussi di lavoro delle applicazioni e la segnalazione delle assunzioni. ▪ Identificare tendenze positive e negative delle prestazioni e proporre piani di azione pratici per rafforzare i risultati. Team Leadership & Collaboration ▪ Supervise, supporto e sviluppare membri del team di assunzione di ammissione e di altri personale di iscrizione come assegnato. ▪ Stabilire chiare aspettative, priorità, strutture di responsabilità e standard di servizio per il team. ▪ Costruire una cultura ad alte prestazioni, ad alte prestazioni che è studente-centrato, collaborativo, data-aware, resiliente e focalizzato sui risultati. ▪ Fornire feedback regolari, coaching e supporto pratico al personale, mentre modellare l'energia, la reattività e la professionalità attesa del team. ▪ Lavorare a stretto contatto con i colleghi attraverso Marketing, Financial Aid, Affari Studenti, Affari Accademici, Finanza, Avanzamento, Facoltà e partner esterni. ▪ Rappresenta Franklin con professionalità, calore, umiltà e credibilità in ambienti interni ed esterni. Budget & Resource Stewardship ▪ Assist con lo sviluppo e l'amministrazione di budget correlati all'iscrizione, tra cui viaggi di reclutamento, eventi, sistemi, agenzie e altre spese dipartimentali. ▪ Link raccomandazioni di spesa per risultati di iscrizione misurabili e priorità istituzionali. ▪ Valutare l'efficacia delle attività di reclutamento, viaggi, fiere, eventi, campagne, piattaforme, agenti e partnership. ▪ Cerca modi pratici e creativi per raggiungere gli obiettivi di iscrizione con risorse limitate, bilanciando l'ambizione con esecuzione disciplinata. ▪ Eseguire altri compiti come assegnato, coerente con questa posizione, gli obiettivi del dipartimento, e la missione dell'Università. ESPERIENZA E QUALIFICA Franklin sta cercando un leader di iscrizione esperto con un minimo di 7–10 anni di esperienza progressiva nella gestione dell'iscrizione all'istruzione superiore, ammissioni, reclutamento, aiuti finanziari o una zona strettamente correlata, tra cui almeno 3–5 anni in un ruolo di leadership senior, supervisore o team. Il candidato di successo sarà tenuto ad avere conseguito un diploma di laurea; un grado avanzato è fortemente preferito. Inoltre, il candidato di successo possederà il seguente: ▪ Fluency di reclutamento — comprensione diretta del ciclo di reclutamento completo degli studenti, tra cui la gestione del territorio, l'impegno familiare, le relazioni con i consulenti, le visite del campus, gli eventi di reclutamento, la resa ammessa-studente, la strategia di conversione, e le pipeline di laurea e laurea. ▪ Orientamento strategico e pratico — Capacità dimostrata di contribuire a sviluppare ed eseguire piani di iscrizione strategici, in particolare in una piccola o media istituzione, mentre anche la gestione del lavoro quotidiano necessario per implementarli efficacemente. ▪ Competenza dei dati — Capacità dimostrata di utilizzare i dati di registrazione, i report dei imbuti, i sistemi CRM, le dashboard, la segmentazione, gli strumenti di business intelligence e l'analisi di conversione per guidare le decisioni, valutare le prestazioni e migliorare i risultati. ▪ Esperienza ardesia — L'esperienza con ardesia è fortemente preferita. L'esperienza con CRM comparabile, reclutamento degli studenti, o sistemi di gestione dell'iscrizione sarà anche considerato. ▪ Consapevolezza degli aiuti finanziari — Conoscenza del lavoro dell'aiuto finanziario, strategia di borsa di studio, preoccupazioni per la convenienza, lo sconto, il comportamento dei rendimenti, l'aiuto finanziario che sfrutta, la modellazione dei tassi di sconto e il rapporto tra iscrizione e finanze istituzionali. ▪ leadership di squadra — Prova capacità di supervisionare, motivare, coach, e tenere il personale collaborativo e altamente performante responsabile in un ambiente veloce e orientato al servizio, tra cui i team che lavorano in più sedi o fusi orari. ▪ Le competenze di comunicazione — Le eccellenti capacità di comunicazione scritte e orali in inglese sono richieste. La competenza in italiano, francese, tedesco, spagnolo, arabo o un'altra lingua rilevante è un bene. ▪ Prospettive internazionali — Esperienza con il reclutamento internazionale, istruzione superiore degli Stati Uniti, mercati svizzeri o europei, partenariati all'estero, studenti globalmente mobili, o l'istruzione transnazionale è un forte vantaggio. ▪ La comprensione delle arti liberali — La familiarità con il mercato del college di arti liberali e la capacità di articolare la sua proposizione di valore a studenti e famiglie potenziali è fortemente preferita. Competenze chiave per Franklin Leaders ▪ Pensiero strategico ▪ Esecuzione pratica ▪ Leading and inspiring ▪ Autoconsapevolezza ▪ Decisioni informate ▪ Comunicazione interculturale ▪ Servizio orientato agli studenti ▪ Collaborazione ▪ Efficienza ▪ Missione continua in evoluzione FRANKLIN SWITZERLAND La missione di Franklin Svizzera è di fornire un ambiente di apprendimento e di vita interculturale e multinazionale che ispira gli studenti a coinvolgere il mondo. Sfidiamo gli studenti attraverso un curriculum che integra le arti liberali con percorsi professionali, e l'apprendimento in classe con il viaggio accademico a destinazioni in tutto il mondo. Un'educazione Franklin produce pensatori critici che sono culturalmente letterati, eticamente consapevoli e intellettualmente coraggiosi. Prepariamo gli studenti a diventare responsabili, compassionevoli e leader collaborativi in un mondo sempre più complesso e interconnesso. Storia Era la fine degli anni Sessanta, e Fleming College, un programma della American School in Svizzera, stava chiudendo le sue porte. Quattro dei suoi docenti, Theo Brenner, Wilfried Geens, Pascal Tone e Jacques Villaret hanno collaborato con la cattedra europea di Fleming per fondare un nuovo istituto di istruzione superiore chiamato Benjamin Franklin. Essi credevano che fornendo esperienze internazionali agli studenti, Franklin College avrebbe rafforzato i rapporti tra membri di diverse nazioni e culture. Pascal Tone trascorse l'estate del 1970 reclutando la prima classe a New York City mentre gli altri completarono la preparazione del primo campus a Villa Cirla, un edificio del XVIII secolo a Lugano. Quell'anno, Franklin ha impiegato 10 docenti e ha offerto 36 corsi sotto 4 soggetti: Studio di Civilizzazioni, Arte, Politica ed Economia, e Lingue e Letteratura. David R. Grace è stato Primo Presidente del Consiglio. Negli anni Settanta, Franklin si trasferì a Villa Ferrari e poi a Villa Sassa, dove fu accreditato per la prima volta come collegio biennale dalla Commissione per l'istruzione superiore (MSCHE). Nel 1986 il Franklin College Svizzera ha finalmente preso residenza nel suo campus permanente in Via Ponte Tresa a Sorengo. Nello stesso anno è stato accreditato come un college di quattro anni dalla MSCHE. Il nuovo millennio ha portato nuova crescita, come tutta la comunità accademica e amministrativa ha cercato di definire un nuovo futuro per Franklin. Nel 2005, i programmi di laurea di Franklin hanno ricevuto l'accreditamento dalla conferenza universitaria svizzera, e nel 2006, il college si è espanso a un secondo campus precedentemente occupato dalla scuola Leonardo DaVinci. Nel 2010 è stato creato il primo master di Franklin. 2013 ha visto Franklin ricevere l'accreditamento istituzionale completo dalla Conferenza universitaria svizzera, rendendolo un istituto di istruzione superiore riconosciuto all'interno del sistema universitario svizzero e l'unico istituto di istruzione superiore al mondo pienamente accreditato sia negli Stati Uniti che in Svizzera. Nel 2023, Franklin aprì il McNeely Center of Ideas & Imagination e il Giardino di Luce. Nominato dopo Rosemary McNeely e Kevin W. McNeely ’73, Trustee, il Centro offre uno spazio per gli studenti di impegnarsi e rafforzare la loro formazione interdisciplinare ed esperienziale a Franklin. Fornendo un volto altamente visibile per l'Università, la facciata rappresenta l'esterno di un libro, un'ode per l'istruzione e l'apprendimento, e comprende molte aree di vita e di apprendimento per la comunità Franklin. Il P. Gregory Warden Student Center, al piano terra, comprende una zona lounge con mobili comodi e modulari, che consente agli studenti di riunirsi, studiare e rilassarsi. Il Giardino di Luce, creato e donato da Nora McNeely Hurley ’81, è uno speciale giardino benessere con più di 24 tipi di lussureggiante flora locale sul versante naturalmente terrazzato. Il giardino comprende uno spazio tra tutte e tre le residenze e funge da ambiente di apprendimento olistico. Fin dalla sua apertura, il McNeely Center of Ideas & Imagination è diventato un hub vibrante nel campus. Nel 2025, Franklin si rinominò ufficialmente e divenne Franklin Svizzera. Dall'inizio dei quattro fondatori che credono nella loro idea di creare un nuovo tipo di istruzione superiore, Franklin occupa ora 9 edifici, tra cui 6 sale di soggiorno, e insegna studenti di oltre 55 paesi che si specializzano in una qualsiasi delle 19 discipline su due campus collegati. I valori fondamentali, tuttavia, sono sempre rimasti gli stessi: l'apprendimento personalizzato attraverso le interazioni sia all'interno che all'esterno dell'aula, la vera comprensione delle persone e delle culture attraverso il contatto diretto e il viaggio guidato, e l'impegno attivo con il mondo come imperativo dell'educazione globale e liberale. Academic & Student Life Franklin Svizzera offre un senso di comunità, interazioni indimenticabili studente-professore, un campus mozzafiato, infinite opportunità derivanti dalla sua posizione centrale in Europa, esperienze accademiche uniche all'interno e all'esterno della classe, l'esposizione e l'integrazione delle culture degli studenti, e una forte rete globale di alunni. Gli studenti di Franklin provengono da 60 paesi diversi. Di conseguenza, diventare uno studente Franklin significa studiare in un ambiente globale vivendo nel cuore dell'Europa e connettersi con le persone in tutto il mondo come studente, non come turista. Franklin offre un'esperienza accademica incredibile che contribuirà alla crescita personale e professionale di ogni studente. La Svizzera ha quattro lingue nazionali: tedesco, francese, italiano e romancio, ma l'inglese è ampiamente parlato, in particolare nelle università, nelle imprese internazionali e nelle principali città. Tutti i programmi accademici a Franklin Svizzera sono insegnati interamente in inglese. Allo stesso tempo, gli studenti sono incoraggiati a sviluppare la competenza in una delle lingue nazionali della Svizzera, rafforzando sia la loro comprensione culturale che le opportunità di carriera. A Franklin Svizzera, gli studenti hanno una serie unica di opportunità accademiche, a partire dal programma di firma di Franklin, Academic Travel. Academic Travel fonde la preparazione dell'aula con l'opportunità di studiare con professori in un paese diverso per due settimane ogni semestre. Questa non è l'unica cosa che distingue Franklin, tuttavia. I professori utilizzano esperienze nel mondo reale per insegnare le competenze pratiche che gli studenti hanno bisogno nella loro carriera. Franklin ospita esperti del settore per discutere interattivamente le tendenze attuali ed emergenti. La facoltà internazionale di Franklin e il corpo studentesco forniscono un ambiente immersivo di prospettive interculturali. Ogni momento trascorso nel campus, sia studiare o rilassarsi, diventa un'esperienza di apprendimento. Franklin offre eventi multiculturali, club e attività per aiutare gli studenti a crescere competenze e fiducia internazionali. Inoltre, Franklin offre opportunità di onorare gli studenti, per gli studenti che possono avere bisogno di una preparazione aggiuntiva, e per le persone sfollate che hanno bisogno di un ulteriore supporto per iniziare o continuare lo studio universitario. Franklin Svizzera offre agli studenti un ambiente di apprendimento unico e dinamico, dove l'istruzione va oltre i confini tradizionali. I laureati possono esplorare una miriade di grandi campi di studio che sono profondamente intrecciati con un approccio interdisciplinare ed esperienziale. La sua vasta gamma di major incorpora diverse discipline come le relazioni internazionali, studi ambientali, economia e arte, permettendo agli studenti di ricevere un'educazione olistica e globale. La flessibilità del curriculum consente agli studenti di modellare il loro percorso accademico, intrecciando i loro interessi e aspirazioni di carriera. A Franklin Svizzera, credono nel potere trasformativo di combinare la teoria accademica con la pratica del mondo reale. Il suo approccio interdisciplinare assicura che gli studenti esplorano soggetti da molteplici prospettive, promuovendo il pensiero critico, problem-solving e una comprensione più approfondita delle questioni globali. I componenti di apprendimento esperienziale permettono agli studenti di impegnarsi in esperienze pratiche, stage e studi sul campo, collegando la conoscenza dell'aula alle applicazioni del mondo reale e migliorando la loro disponibilità professionale. LOCAZIONE Lugano Il campus Franklin si trova su una collina a Sorengo, sopra la città di Lugano, nel sud della Svizzera. Situato nella regione di lingua italiana, gli studenti, la facoltà e il personale possono godere di un'atmosfera mediterranea rimanendo legati alle principali città europee. La città trasuda fascino italiano; lo stile di vita mediterraneo sul lago di Lugano, in combinazione con le montagne circostanti, rendono Lugano una destinazione popolare. Lugano è il polo culturale, ricreativo, finanziario e commerciale del cantone più meridionale della Svizzera, di lingua italiana del Ticino, il vaso di fusione ideale della cultura europea combinato con i tratti di una piccola città. È divertente, sofisticato e sicuro, con decine di attività all'aperto intorno al Lago di Lugano, tra cui 40 delle migliori mountain bike d'Europa. I residenti possono godere del centro della città con piazze e portici in stile mediterraneo, numerosi parchi e ogni varietà di negozi e ristoranti, così come il LAC Lugano Arte e Cultura, il nuovo Arts Center di Lugano dove arti visive, musica e arti performative si incontrano in un unico luogo in modo da fornire la migliore esperienza d'arte in ogni forma. Questi e altri eventi rinomati attirano visitatori da tutta Europa. Di conseguenza, il francese, il tedesco e l’inglese sono probabilmente sentiti per le strade, oltre al nativo italiano della città. Lugano è il punto centrale di partenza per tutta l'Europa. Con le linee ferroviarie e l’aeroporto regionale di Lugano, tutta l’Europa è facilmente raggiungibile. Solo un'ora di viaggio da Lugano è Milano, il centro commerciale del nord Italia — e con poche ore aggiuntive, raggiungere Venezia, Firenze, Strasburgo, Nizza e Innsbruck. Svizzera Situata nel cuore dell'Europa, la Svizzera confina con Italia, Francia, Germania, Austria e Liechtenstein. Uno dei paesi più belli del mondo con le sue montagne sorprendenti e paesaggi mozzafiato, la Svizzera è riconosciuta a livello mondiale per la sua innovazione, stabilità politica, sistema educativo eccezionale e qualità eccezionale della vita. La Svizzera è anche costantemente classificata tra i paesi più sicuri del mondo, offrendo un'alta qualità di vita e servizi pubblici eccellenti. La sua infrastruttura ben organizzata e i tassi di criminalità bassi lo rendono una destinazione attraente. Come un melting pot culturale con quattro lingue ufficiali (tedesco, francese, italiano e romancio), un sostenitore della partecipazione globale, e un noto hub per l'efficienza, la Svizzera è una grande scelta per i professionisti che cercano di muoversi all'estero. Franklin Svizzera offre un pacchetto di compensazione competitivo, tra cui assistenza di trasferimento, e un salario commisurato con qualifiche ed esperienza. La gamma identificata per questo ruolo è di 130.000 – 150.000 franchi svizzeri / 160.000 – 185.000 dollari statunitensi. Si tratta di una posizione a tempo pieno e on-campus con sede a Lugano, Svizzera. I candidati possono aspettarsi un ambiente di lavoro accogliente, internazionale e interculturale e accademico, pieno di un forte senso di compagnia e appartenenza. Le offerte di lavoro saranno condizionate a risultati soddisfacenti di un controllo di fondo. A APPLY NES, una società di ricerca esecutiva nazionale specializzata nell'istruzione superiore, è Franklin Svizzera con questa ricerca di un Vicepresidente per la gestione delle iscrizioni. Se si desidera avere una conversazione confidenziale su questa opportunità o presentare candidature, si prega di contattare: Laura Robinson (laura.robinson@nessearches.com) o Drew Nichols (drew.nichols@nessearches.com). Per applicare, si prega di inviare i seguenti articoli via e-mail a: francnklin@nessearches.com: 1) un curriculum che dettaglia l'esperienza rilevante; 2) una lettera di interesse che affronta le aree chiave di questa descrizione del lavoro e spiega perché Franklin Svizzera è un prossimo passo convincente, e 3) informazioni di contatto per cinque riferimenti professionali. Per una migliore considerazione, tutti i materiali di applicazione devono essere presentati elettronicamente entro il 14 ottobre 2026. Tutte le richieste, le candidature e le domande saranno gestite con la massima riservatezza e i candidati saranno notificati prima che vengano contattati i riferimenti. La data di inizio prevista del VPEM non è più tardi del gennaio 2027. * Si prega di notare che, a causa del visto svizzero e del regolamento di lavoro-permesso, le domande da cittadini svizzeri o UE saranno date priorità nel processo di valutazione. Franklin Svizzera è un Equal Opportunity / Azione Affermativa datore di lavoro, e tutti i candidati qualificati riceveranno considerazione per l'occupazione senza riguardo a età, razza, colore, religione, sesso, orientamento sessuale, identità di genere o espressione, origine nazionale, stato di disabilità, stato veterano protetto, o qualsiasi altra caratteristica protetta dalla legge. descriptionByLocale.en: Franklin Switzerland, founded in 1969, is one of the first institutions to bring liberal arts education to Europe and to be recognized by both U.S. and Swiss accreditation agencies. A leader in international education, Franklin provides an experiential and multinational learning environment through small classes, strong student and faculty relationships, a residential campus, and hands-on Academic Travel experiences. With roughly 300 students from more than 55 countries, set in the safe and striking landscape of Lugano, Franklin is distinctive: an intimate residential community, a uniquely dual U.S.–Swiss accreditation, and an Academic Travel program that turns the world into a classroom. Franklin promotes intellectual curiosity and critical thinking, strives for academic excellence, and fosters interdisciplinary opportunities for its students, faculty, and staff. Franklin acknowledges the accomplishments and global impact of our community through a culture of trust that respects representation from a variety of backgrounds, as well as an environment that strives for continuous improvement. THE OPPORTUNITY Franklin Switzerland is seeking an accomplished, hands-on, and strategically minded Vice President of Enrollment Management (VPEM) to help lead student recruitment, admissions operations, financial-aid coordination, and enrollment growth at a pivotal moment for the University. This is an important institutional role for someone who understands both the human and analytical sides of enrollment. Franklin needs a person who can think strategically, act practically, manage people and processes, work comfortably with data, and remain close to the daily work of recruitment and conversion. The successful candidate will bring energy, judgment, discipline, and a genuine belief in the value of a Franklin education. The VPEM will work closely with the President, senior leadership, Admissions, Financial Aid, Marketing and Communications, Academic Affairs, Student Affairs, Finance, faculty, staff, students, external partners, agents, and school counselors to support Franklin’s enrollment goals across undergraduate, graduate, transfer, visiting, study abroad, and partnership pathways. This is not a role for someone who wants only to supervise from a distance. It requires a leader who can build systems, coach staff, review data, improve communication flows, speak with families, support recruitment travel, solve practical problems, and help move prospective students from interest to enrollment. Franklin is looking for a VPEM who is genuinely fluent across the enrollment cycle and who can hold three priorities in balance: Recruitment and conversion — building a disciplined, warm, and responsive admissions operation that supports students and families from first inquiry through application, admission, deposit, visa, arrival, and handoff to the student experience. Data and systems — using Slate, funnel reports, dashboards, segmentation, and timely analysis to identify opportunities, address weaknesses, improve conversion, and support evidence-based enrollment decisions. Collaboration and execution — working across departments to ensure that Franklin’s distinctive academic, residential, and international identity is translated into clear recruitment messages, effective campaigns, strong events, and a consistent prospective-student experience. The ideal candidate understands that enrollment management is both strategic and practical. Students and families make decisions over time, through many interactions, questions, doubts, comparisons, and moments of reassurance. Franklin must be visible, compelling, responsive, credible, and operationally excellent throughout that journey. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Enrollment Strategy & Planning ▪ Support the development, implementation, and evaluation of a comprehensive enrollment management plan aligned with Franklin’s mission, academic priorities, financial realities, and strategic goals. ▪ Translate enrollment goals into practical recruitment plans, territory strategies, communication flows, event calendars, staff priorities, funnel targets, and measurable outcomes. ▪ Monitor enrollment trends, application behavior, deposit patterns, yield indicators, market conditions, and competitor activity, and recommend timely adjustments. ▪ Work closely with senior leadership to support short- and long-term enrollment planning, including undergraduate, graduate, transfer, visiting, study abroad, and partnership enrollment. ▪ Contribute to regular enrollment reporting for the President, senior leadership, relevant committees, and other internal stakeholders. ▪ Help foster a campus-wide culture of enrollment awareness, shared responsibility, openness, and precision. Recruitment, Admissions & Yield ▪ Lead and support the admissions recruitment team in achieving inquiry, application, admit, deposit, and enrollment goals. ▪ Oversee the prospective-student journey from inquiry to enrollment, ensuring timely, professional, warm, and persuasive communication with students, families, counselors, agents, and partners. ▪ Strengthen recruitment practices, admissions processes, territory management, school counselor outreach, campus visits, virtual engagement, admitted-student yield, and pre-arrival communication. ▪ Personally engage in recruitment activity where needed, including conversations with prospective students and families, school visits, fairs, partner meetings, admitted-student events, and yield initiatives. ▪ Work closely with Marketing and Communications to ensure that recruitment campaigns, landing pages, email flows, social content, events, and digital outreach are aligned with enrollment priorities and Franklin’s distinctive identity. ▪ Support strategies to grow enrollment across specific programs and markets, and to sustain Franklin's signature multinational classroom, often 15–20 nationalities represented in a single course, by recruiting broadly across countries and regions and by broadening access for students from a range of socioeconomic backgrounds. ▪ Contribute to the development of study abroad, visiting-student, transfer, and institutional partnership pipelines. ▪ Regular travel may be required, including recruitment travel, school visits, fairs, conferences, partner meetings, and engagement with students, families, counselors, agents, alumni, and institutional partners in Switzerland, Europe, the United States, and other relevant markets. Financial Aid & Affordability ▪ Work closely with the Director of Financial Aid to ensure that financial-aid processes are timely, clear, student-centered, compliant, and aligned with enrollment goals. ▪ Support financial-aid and scholarship strategies that balance access, affordability, yield, net tuition revenue, discount rate, and institutional sustainability. ▪ Help analyze financial-aid data, award behavior, yield patterns, family concerns, and affordability barriers to support improved enrollment outcomes. ▪ Ensure that students and families receive accurate, clear, and supportive guidance on cost, aid, payment expectations, and the value of a Franklin education. ▪ Partner with Finance and senior leadership as needed to support enrollment forecasting, financial-aid modeling, and net revenue analysis. Data, Slate & Enrollment Operations ▪ Use Slate and other enrollment technologies to support recruitment, admissions processing, communications, reporting, events, application review, and yield management. ▪ Develop and maintain clear enrollment dashboards, funnel reports, conversion analyses, and regular performance updates. ▪ Ensure that data quality, coding, source tracking, communication rules, forms, workflows, and reporting structures support accurate analysis and effective decision-making. ▪ Recommend and implement process improvements to increase speed, clarity, responsiveness, user experience, data quality, and access to services. ▪ Collaborate with the Slate Manager and relevant colleagues to improve automation, communication plans, event management, application workflows, and recruitment reporting. ▪ Identify positive and negative performance trends and propose practical action plans to strengthen results. Team Leadership & Collaboration ▪ Supervise, support, and develop members of the admissions recruitment team and other enrollment staff as assigned. ▪ Establish clear expectations, priorities, accountability structures, and service standards for the team. ▪ Build a high-trust, high-performance culture that is student-centered, collaborative, data-aware, resilient, and focused on results. ▪ Provide regular feedback, coaching, and practical support to staff, while modeling the energy, responsiveness, and professionalism expected of the team. ▪ Work closely with colleagues across Marketing, Financial Aid, Student Affairs, Academic Affairs, Finance, Advancement, faculty, and external partners. ▪ Represent Franklin with professionalism, warmth, humility, and credibility in internal and external settings. Budget & Resource Stewardship ▪ Assist with the development and administration of enrollment-related budgets, including recruitment travel, events, systems, agencies, and other departmental expenditures. ▪ Link spending recommendations to measurable enrollment outcomes and institutional priorities. ▪ Evaluate the effectiveness of recruitment activities, travel, fairs, events, campaigns, platforms, agents, and partnerships. ▪ Seek practical and creative ways to achieve enrollment goals with limited resources, balancing ambition with disciplined execution. ▪ Perform other duties as assigned, consistent with this position, the department’s goals, and the University’s mission. EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS Franklin is seeking an experienced enrollment leader with a minimum of 7–10 years of progressive experience in higher education enrollment management, admissions, recruitment, financial aid, or a closely related area, including at least 3–5 years in a senior, supervisory, or team leadership role. The successful candidate will be required to have earned a bachelor’s degree; an advanced degree is strongly preferred. In addition, the successful candidate will possess the following: ▪ Recruitment fluency — Direct understanding of the full student recruitment cycle, including territory management, family engagement, counselor relationships, campus visits, recruitment events, admitted-student yield, conversion strategy, and undergraduate and graduate pipelines. ▪ Strategic and practical orientation — Demonstrated ability to help develop and execute strategic enrollment plans, particularly in a small or mid-sized institution, while also managing the daily work required to implement them effectively. ▪ Data competence — Demonstrated ability to use enrollment data, funnel reports, CRM systems, dashboards, segmentation, business intelligence tools, and conversion analysis to guide decisions, evaluate performance, and improve outcomes. ▪ Slate experience — Experience with Slate is strongly preferred. Experience with comparable CRM, student recruitment, or enrollment management systems will also be considered. ▪ Financial-aid awareness — Working knowledge of financial aid, scholarship strategy, affordability concerns, discounting, yield behavior, financial aid leveraging, discount rate modeling, and the relationship between enrollment and institutional finances. ▪ Team leadership — Proven ability to supervise, motivate, coach, and hold accountable collaborative, high-performing staff in a fast-moving and service-oriented environment, including teams working across multiple locations or time zones. ▪ Communication skills — Excellent written and oral communication skills in English are required. A Franklin education produces critical thinkers who are culturally literate, ethically aware and intellectually courageous. History It was the end of the sixties, and Fleming College, a program of The American School in Switzerland, was closing its doors. Four of its faculty, Theo Brenner, Wilfried Geens, Pascal Tone and Jacques Villaret teamed up with the chair of Fleming’s European board to found a new higher education institution named after Benjamin Franklin. They believed that by providing international experiences to students, Franklin College would strengthen the relationships between members of different nations and cultures. Pascal Tone spent the summer of 1970 recruiting the first class in New York City while the others completed preparation of the first campus at Villa Cirla, an 18th century building in Lugano. That year, Franklin employed 10 faculty and offered 36 courses under 4 subjects: Study of Civilizations, Art, Politics and Economics, and Languages and Literature. David R. Grace served as First Chairman of the Board. During the seventies, Franklin moved to Villa Ferrari and then to Villa Sassa, where it was first accredited as a two-year college by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education (MSCHE). In 1986 Franklin College Switzerland finally took residence in its permanent campus on Via Ponte Tresa in Sorengo. In that same year it was accredited as a four-year college by the MSCHE. The new millennium brought new growth, as the entire academic and administrative community sought to define a new future for Franklin. In 2005, Franklin's undergraduate programs received accreditation from the Swiss University Conference, and in 2006, the college expanded to a second campus formerly occupied by the Leonardo DaVinci school. In 2010, Franklin’s first master’s degree program was created. 2013 saw Franklin receive full institutional accreditation from the Swiss University Conference, making it a recognized higher education institution within the Swiss university system and the only higher education institution in the world fully accredited in both the US and Switzerland. In 2023, Franklin opened the McNeely Center of Ideas & Imagination and the Giardino di Luce. Named after Rosemary McNeely and Kevin W. McNeely ’73, Trustee, the Center offers a space for students to engage and strengthen their interdisciplinary and experiential education at Franklin. Providing a highly visible face for the University, the facade represents the exterior of a book, an ode to education and learning, and includes many living and learning areas for the Franklin community. The ground floor’s P. Gregory Warden Student Center, comprises a lounge area with comfortable, modular furniture, allowing students to come together, study, and relax. The Giardino di Luce, or Garden of Light, created and donated by Nora McNeely Hurley ’81, is a special wellness garden filled with more than 24 types of lush local flora in the naturally terraced slope. The garden encompasses a space between all three residences and serves as a holistic learning environment. Since its opening, the McNeely Center of Ideas & Imagination has become a vibrant hub on campus. In 2025, Franklin officially renamed itself and became Franklin Switzerland. From the beginning of the four founders believing in their idea to create a new kind of higher education, Franklin now occupies 9 buildings, including 6 residence halls, and teaches students from over 55 countries majoring in any of 19 disciplines on two connected campuses. The fundamental values, however, have always remained the same: personalized learning through interactions both inside and outside of the classroom, true understanding of people and cultures through direct contact and guided travel, and active engagement with the world as an imperative of global, liberal education. Academic & Student Life Franklin Switzerland offers a sense of community, unforgettable student-professor interactions, a breathtaking campus, endless opportunities deriving from its central location in Europe, unique academic experiences inside and outside of the classroom, the exposure and integration of student cultures, and a strong global alumni network. Franklin students originate from 60 different countries. As a result, becoming a Franklin student means studying in a global environment while living in the heart of Europe and connecting with people worldwide as a student, not as a tourist. Franklin provides an incredible academic experience that will contribute to each student’s personal and professional growth. Switzerland has four national languages—German, French, Italian, and Romansh—but English is widely spoken, particularly in universities, international businesses, and major cities. All academic programs at Franklin Switzerland are taught entirely in English. At the same time, students are encouraged to develop proficiency in one of Switzerland's national languages, strengthening both their cultural understanding and career opportunities. At Franklin Switzerland, students have a unique set of academic opportunities, starting with Franklin’s signature program, Academic Travel. Academic Travel blends classroom preparation with the opportunity to study with professors in a different country for two weeks every semester. That isn’t the only thing that sets Franklin apart, however. Professors use real-world experiences to teach the practical skills students need in their careers. Franklin hosts industry experts to interactively discuss current and emerging trends. Franklin’s international faculty and student body provide an immersive environment of cross-cultural perspectives. Every moment spent on campus, whether studying or relaxing, becomes a learning experience. Franklin offers multicultural events, clubs, and activities to help students grow international competence and confidence. What’s more, Franklin offers opportunities for honors students, for students who may need some additional preparation, and for displaced persons needing additional support to begin or continue university study. Franklin Switzerland offers students a unique and dynamic learning environment, where education goes beyond traditional boundaries. Undergraduates can explore a myriad of major fields of study that are deeply intertwined with an interdisciplinary and experiential approach. Its diverse array of majors incorporates various disciplines such as international relations, environmental studies, economics, and art, allowing students to receive a holistic and globally oriented education. The flexibility of the curriculum enables students to shape their academic journey, intertwining their interests and career aspirations. At Franklin Switzerland, they believe in the transformative power of combining academic theory with real-world practice. Its interdisciplinary approach ensures that students explore subjects from multiple perspectives, fostering critical thinking, problem-solving, and a deeper understanding of global issues. The experiential learning components allow students to engage in practical experiences, internships, and field studies, connecting classroom knowledge to real-world applications and enhancing their professional readiness. LOCATION Lugano The Franklin campus is located on a hillside in Sorengo, above the city of Lugano, in the south of Switzerland. Nestled in the Italian-speaking region, students, faculty, and staff can enjoy a Mediterranean atmosphere while remaining connected to major European cities. The city exudes Italian charm; the Mediterranean lifestyle on Lake Lugano, in combination with the surrounding mountains, make Lugano a popular destination. Lugano is the cultural, recreational, financial, and commercial hub of Switzerland’s southernmost, Italian-speaking canton of Ticino, the ideal melting pot of European culture combined with the traits of a small town. It is fun, sophisticated and safe, with dozens of outdoor activities around Lake Lugano, including 40 of Europe’s best mountain bike routes. Residents can enjoy the city center with Mediterranean-style squares and arcades, numerous parks and every variety of shops and restaurants, as well as the LAC Lugano Arte e Cultura, Lugano’s new Arts Center where visual arts, music and performing arts come together in a single venue so as to provide the best experience of art in every form. Franklin Schweiz, gegründet 1969, ist eine der ersten Institutionen, die liberale Kunstausbildung nach Europa bringt und sowohl von US-amerikanischen als auch von Schweizer Akkreditierungsagenturen anerkannt wird. Als führendes Unternehmen in der internationalen Bildung bietet Franklin eine experimentelle und multinationale Lernumgebung durch kleine Klassen, starke Studenten- und Dozentenbeziehungen, einen Wohncampus und praktische akademische Reiseerfahrungen. Mit rund 300 Studenten aus mehr als 55 Ländern, die sich in der sicheren und beeindruckenden Landschaft von Lugano befinden, ist Franklin unverwechselbar: eine intime Wohngemeinschaft, eine einzigartig duale Akkreditierung zwischen den USA und der Schweiz und ein akademisches Reiseprogramm, das die Welt in ein Klassenzimmer verwandelt. Franklin fördert intellektuelle Neugier und kritisches Denken, strebt nach akademischer Exzellenz und fördert interdisziplinäre Möglichkeiten für seine Studenten, Dozenten und Mitarbeiter. Franklin würdigt die Errungenschaften und globalen Auswirkungen unserer Gemeinschaft durch eine Kultur des Vertrauens, die Repräsentation aus einer Vielzahl von Hintergründen respektiert, sowie ein Umfeld, das nach kontinuierlicher Verbesserung strebt. Franklin Schweiz ist auf der Suche nach einem gelungenen, praxisorientierten und strategisch denkenden Vice President of Enrollment Management (VPEM), um die Rekrutierung von Studenten, Zulassungsoperationen, die Koordination von Finanzhilfen und das Einschreibungswachstum zu einem entscheidenden Zeitpunkt für die Universität zu unterstützen. Dies ist eine wichtige institutionelle Rolle für jemanden, der sowohl die menschliche als auch die analytische Seite der Einschreibung versteht. Franklin braucht eine Person, die strategisch denken, praktisch handeln, Menschen und Prozesse verwalten, bequem mit Daten arbeiten und nah an der täglichen Arbeit der Rekrutierung und Konversion bleiben kann. Der erfolgreiche Kandidat wird Energie, Urteilsvermögen, Disziplin und einen echten Glauben an den Wert einer Franklin-Ausbildung bringen. Die VPEM wird eng mit dem Präsidenten, der leitenden Führung, Zulassungen, Finanzhilfe, Marketing und Kommunikation, Akademische Angelegenheiten, Student Affairs, Finanzen, Dozenten, Mitarbeiter, Studenten, externen Partnern, Agenten und Schulberatern zusammenarbeiten, um Franklins Einschreibungsziele für Studenten, Absolventen, Transfer, Besuch, Auslandsstudium und Partnerschaftswege zu unterstützen.
